user_questions.question: Two intent questions. (1) Who are 'support agents'? Options: (a) users on 'Custom: Support Profile' (internal Salesforce license; has Case Delete=true, no Refund__c access; 0 users today) [recommended]; (b) the Agentforce service agent ('Einstein Agent User'; no Case/Refund__c access); (c) the guest support profiles ('Customer Support Profile', 'Merchant Support Profile'; no Case/Refund__c access); (d) all of these. (2) For 'Ever': (a) remove Delete from support-agent profiles and permission sets (standard access control; a later grant could re-enable it) or (b) additionally add a before-delete guard that blocks deletes even if Delete is granted later? Recommendation: (a) plus governance, since no automation deletes these records today.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Remove Delete on Case and Refund from agent profiles/perm sets.

skill_friction: Profile API naming: spec-format says 'use full metadata API names' but gives no guidance for profiles whose fullName is URL-encoded (Custom%3A Support Profile) vs the label; I used the encoded fullName in Section 4/9 and mentioned the label.

'Ever' is a strength-of-enforcement cue: SKILL.md step 5 does not say whether enforcement strength (permission removal vs hard before-delete guard) is intent (ask) or implementation (decide). I asked, bundled with the persona question.

Two-wrong-claims rule triggered after D1/D2 (Support Profile Case Delete reported false, actually true; C2C* sets reported with Case Delete, none found), yet AskCoworker kept labelling stale 'prior session' facts in I/R/T; the rule says verify every kept fact but gives no guidance on whether R/T should still be sent once AskCoworker is known unreliable.

Persona with zero users: the skill has no case for a design whose target profile has 0 users (requirement effectively preventive); unclear if that is 'already met', a partly false premise, or a normal change. Treated as a normal change plus a load-bearing assumption.
Answer mapping: the simulated answer ('agent profiles/perm sets') addressed Q2 but not the Q1 options; mapping rule applied (evidence favours Custom: Support Profile), tagged assumption.
